sweep_summary: Groma (grom1238) is not in the catalog. the list of works with stress in the title held one item, An 2007b 'Syntax at the PF interface', which is a generative syntax-phonology-interface thesis with no bearing on Groma: Glottolog attached it (with the other 'PF' items) to Groma through a keyword match on the typo 'purpose pf comparison' in Walsh 1905's title, and the DOI on the record resolves on Crossref to Arregi & Nevins 2013. No first-hand statement of Groma word stress could be read anywhere: Walsh 1905 (the only Groma-specific description; pronunciation notes on p. vi as summarised by Yliniemi 2021 and the 1906 JRAS notice cover vowels and consonants only) is print-only; Zong & bSam gtan 2024 (the only modern phonology of Yadong/Groma; abstract says the dialect has lexical tones) is behind NCPSSD/CNKI login; Tournadre & Suzuki 2023 give only family-level statements (S section 'generally two distinctive pitch tones'; trochaic pattern in most tonal dialects, Dromo not named); CDTD is paywalled.org, Google Books, De Gruyter, Bing, cqvip, HathiTrust). Evidence records and. Acquisition priority: Zong & bSam gtan 2024 full text (high), Walsh 1905 print (medium).

The Zong & bSam-gtan 2024 abstr…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Groma/Dromo is described only as a tonal Southern-Tibetic (Dzongkha-Lhoke section) variety with a two-way pitch-tone (register) contrast; no source that could be opened states where word stress falls in Dromo specifically. The family-level default given by Tournadre & Suzuki (7.3.4, p. 242) for tonal Tibetic dialects incl. Dzongkha is a trochaic (strong-weak) pattern over the first two syllables with tone borne on the first syllable, but this is not asserted for Dromo by name.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Dromo. T&S note stress is at most a secondary feature in tonal dialects (7.3.3).
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level (S section) suprasegmental statement, not a Dromo-specific word-prosody description; the dedicated 2024 description's tone section could not be read.
new_statements.identity_note: Groma [gro] = Dromo གྲོ་མོ་ (Tournadre & Suzuki), Tromowa (Walsh), 亚东话/卓木话 Yadong Tibetan (Chinese literature), spoken in Dromo/Yadong County (Chumbi valley), TAR; Glottolog dialects Upper Groma uppe1409 / Lower Groma lowe1398 = T&S Upper/Lower Dromo. Zong & bSam-gtan 2024 describe '亚东话' without (in the abstract) specifying Upper vs Lower. T&S's quoted suprasegmental statement is for the whole S section (Dzongkha nucl1307-group, Lhoke sikk1242, Dromo), not Dromo alone.

sources.quote: Yliniemi 2021 fn. 8: "Walsh (1905: vi) lists some ways in which Tromowa pronunciation differs from Central Tibetan. Three are listed here. The first is the neutralization of the difference ãː vs õː so that only õː is used. ... The second difference is the pronunciation of WT glide y as separate from the bilabial plosive (e.g. pja) ... The third difference ... is the tendency to replace the Central Tibetan glide r with y, i.e. kja 'hair'"
